segments: Chronography of Bar Hebraeus.
...were eager to kill the head of their religion.
Then, when Mas'ud directed his course to Azerbaijan to wage war with David his brother's son,
he took the Caliph along with him.
And again Sanjar sent ambassadors to Mas'ud while he was encamped at the gate of the city of Maragha,
and urged him without delay to send the Caliph to Baghdad.
And there also came numerous forces from Sanjar,
and with them seventeen Ishmaelite men.
And on Thursday at the time of noon, the sixteenth
of the eleventh month of the year 1439 [of the Greeks],
529 of the Arabs,
while he was sitting and reading in their book inside the tent,
fifteen men entered upon him,
having knives in their hands,
and they killed him,
and with him three others of his nobles.
Mas'ud, however, mounted his horse and surrounded the tents,
and they killed his murderers.
And some say
that Sanjar was unaware of the Ishmaelites; but the truth is
that he had sent them,
while Mas'ud was unaware.
After Mustarshid, Rashid his son [ruled] one year.
For when the Caliph Mustarshid was killed,
Sultan Sanjar sent to the governor of Baghdad,
and ordered that the nobles and judges should assemble and proclaim Rashid, the son of Mustarshid, as Caliph,
and seat him in his father's place.
And so they did.
And at that time that Dubays bar Sadaqa also acted deceitfully against Sultan Mas'ud,
and wrote a letter to Zengi, saying:
"Behold, I am scheming to get away from this man's presence,
and I will come to you,
and assemble {or: assemble!} the forces of the Ma'addites like the sand on the seashore,
and the two of us will unite,
and do with Mas'ud a deed to be remembered by the generations to come."
Now that letter fell into the hands of someone who brought it to {OCR: read ܠܡܲܤܥܘܼܕ} Mas'ud.
Then on a certain day, when the nobles were gathered to him,
and he had given them date-wine to drink according to custom,
and they rose up to go out,
the Sultan signaled to Dubays:
"Wait,
I have a secret matter [to discuss] with you."
And when those men went out,
and Dubays remained,
Mas'ud arose and entered the inner pavilion,
and gave a certain letter to an Armenian servant bearing a sword,
and said to him:
"Go out and hand it to Dubays,
and while he begins to read,
you, from behind him,"
